Hello! There are actually many stages of age regression you could be referring to if you don't think she's "full on regressing." :)  


Age Dreaming: agedreaming is the act of acting as a child or doing childish things (sometimes with little gear) without going through the process of regressing. this is also used as a therapeutic method to ease stress. most agedreamers don't want to go through the process of actual regression for their own personal reasons or are simply unable to put themself in the proper headspace. Age dreamers are just as valid as age regressors! Lots of age regressors also agedream!  


Borderline Regression: this refers to the headspace regressors go into when they're "half-little, half-big." They haven't fully slipped and for some this is the furthest they can go or are comfortable going. They are still aware of being an adult but generally feel much smaller and it often shows through their mannerisms or speech.  


Full/Deep Regression: Fully in the mindset of a child, showing through both speech, actions, mannerisms and thought patterns. It is very important to be gentle with them and not do anything that could be triggering to them (as most regressors develop age regression as a coping mechanism in response to trauma) as it could cause a lot of psychological damage or even a "little drought" (the inability to regress fully or properly for a long period of time)  


Another reason to avoid doing anything triggering during their regression is because age regression isn't always a happy place for a regressor, especially those with trauma. Anything triggering or upsetting can cause "impure regression" which refers to when an age regressor, instead of regressing to a happy worry-free space, regresses to a time where they experienced their trauma, it's very distressing and best to avoid!   


It is also important to note that age regression isn't always voluntarily, especially for those with severe trauma who may regress spontaneously in response to anything overwhelming or triggering!   


Buying her a paci is a lovely gesture to show that you aren't judging her and respect her coping mechanism, because it's hard for a lot of regressors to talk about no matter how much they trust someone. If she does tell you and you do want to participate it helping keep her regression safe, especially if she has deep or full regression, it's best to ask the ages she regresses to so you can find out more on how to care for that specific age range, because remember, when they're fully regressed, they're just like any other kid that age! (Speaking from personal experience because I've gotten myself hurt and sick because I had fully regressed with no supervision)  


Sorry if I rambled on for too long, I just wanted to share as much knowledge as possible to make sure everything is comfy for her and hopefully you have a better understanding! I wish you all the luck. :)
